dimension_assessments.summary: Required provider identity, drift prevention, vocabulary, graph remediation, seam visibility, lifecycle, and approval behaviors are explicit at requirement level.
The window establishes provider-actor auditability, drift guarding, canonical copy, graph-owned governance, weak-integration presentation, reopen/revoke policy, and runtime-anchored approval.
Named identity fields and UI/policy concepts lack complete field schemas, producer inputs, emitted outputs, and payload shapes.
High-level cross-document contracts are explicit, but actor identity, canonical vocabulary, state-machine, approval, and defect payload contracts remain incomplete.
Named completion, revocation, reopen, blocked, and promotion states exist, but their complete transition graph and guards do not.
Decision_Policy and graph ownership are named, but transition, patch, drift-repair, and approval authorities are not allocated precisely.
Each PlanUnit identifies Decision_Log as owner_doc and lists implementation/owner-hint documents; Decision_Policy explicitly owns lifecycle policy objects and transitions.
Several consumers are named, especially label/action/runtime/object surfaces, but notification, event, replay, analytics, and recovery consumers are not enumerated.
Canonical labels, visible weak-integration summaries, completion distinctions, blocked metadata, and approval framing are explicit, while detailed UI interaction and presentation states remain open.
Blocked context and schema mismatch are exposed, but deterministic recovery for drift, blocked episodes, revocation/reopen, and evidence defects is missing.
Provider account snapshots, actor auditability, execution context, and approval identity are security-sensitive, yet authorization, redaction, retention, and privacy boundaries are not stated.
Dependencies, unblocks, implementation surfaces, and owner hints show intended propagation, but event propagation and consistency semantics across consumers are not defined.
The window does not specify telemetry, alerting, runbooks, reconciliation cadence, or operator workflows for drift, blocked states, schema defects, and replay failures.
No limits, latency targets, pagination/aggregation rules, snapshot-volume strategy, or large-graph UI behavior are defined.
The decisions supersede run_id-only storage, alternate labels, request-centric approval framing, and earlier lifecycle semantics without defining data/copy/state migration or backward compatibility.
Acceptance bullets and plan validators exist, but executable runtime, governance, and GUI oracles are absent.

Substantial discretion remains in identity schemas, vocabularies, state machines, UI interaction, authority, security, migration, recovery, operations, and tests; work-node creation is explicitly deferred.
The most consequential ambiguities are the weak-integration taxonomy mismatch and undefined identity, authority, transition, recovery, and compatibility details.
